findings.description: The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data and the resulting file can expose the credential to principals or processes with access to instance metadata, launch configuration history, or the host filesystem.

The RDS instance is configured with publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is VPC-scoped, public accessibility unnecessarily expands the database attack surface and makes future security-group changes externally consequential.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the database storage and automated backups unencrypted at rest, exposing stored database contents if underlying storage or backup access is compromised.

The EC2-assumable application role is granted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* against every resource. A compromise of aws_instance.catalog_app_server would yield broad account-level control and potential access to or modification of unrelated S3, EC2, and RDS resources.
